messages:
alex: kicking off an nsys quicktrace for the long-seq workload, repro attached. saw a sharp queue-time spike and a kernel fallback around the 30s mark. sharing raw notes.
priya: can you paste the nsys CLI you used?
alex: `nsys profile --trace=cuda,cudnn,nvtx -o /tmp/kv_run.nsys ./bin/infer --workload long-seq --duration 40s`
jamal: load/timeline shows continuous batching window stretched and queue time grows -> kernel selector flips to a generic matmul. p95 queue went 2ms -> 48ms during warmup.
zack: any logs for the selector? fallback reason?
alex: selector log snippet:
```
[WARN] kernel_selector: chosen int8_matmul (id=0x7f) not supported on this SM, falling back -> generic_matmul
[DEBUG] batch_window=12ms | batch_size=18 | seq_len=1024 | sm=86
```
priya: hmm. could be shared memory or workspace threshold. what about KV cache behavior? are KVs being warmed or causing stalls?
jamal: KV access pattern looks hot for popular prefixes. cold misses cause a small CPU-side prep that delays scheduling; this interacts poorly with continuous batching timing.
zack: proposal: try a lightweight kv_prefetch before batching (best-effort) + reduce batch_window for long-seq traffic. tradeoff is extra mem for prefetch.
alex: quick experiment results:
```
config:
  batch_window_ms: 8
  kv_prefetch: true
  prefetch_ttl_ms: 150
results:
  queue_p95: 48ms -> 8ms
  gpu_mem_inc: ~120MB
  p95_total_latency: -14%
```
priya: wow that looks promising. can you repro on CI or staging?
perf-bot: [ALERT] perf-regression detected: pull/ci-3421 long-seq p95 +12% vs baseline. triggered perf test suite.
zack: likely related. CI uses batch_window_ms=10 default; try canary with batch_window_ms=6 and force kernel preference for fast_matmul_fp16 for seq<=1024.
alex: rolling canary: kselector-ttl-20260318 -> staging now. will include kv_prefetch toggle.
deploy-bot: Deploy started for canary/kselector-ttl-20260318 by alex
jamal: quick numbers from staging canary: p95 long-seq +2% vs baseline (better). queue_p95 dropped to ~7ms. kernel_id stabilized to fast_matmul_fp16 for seq<=1024.
priya: please add a regression test that locks seq_len>=1024 and asserts kernel_id==fast_matmul_fp16 and queue_p95<15ms. add perfetto link in the ticket.
alex: adding tests and uploading perfetto trace to the bug. will follow up with a more detailed writeup and thresholds. thanks :thumbsup:\n
